extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of German literature and literary criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Lecture-style critical guidelines for judging and creating German (and national) poetry and literature across generations; emphasizes measures, national elements, style, and the critic's stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a national and familiar measure
rubrics_metrics.description: He who would create a truly national poem must choose a national and familiar measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign or severe elaborate forms can be useful as exercises and to correct careless writing, but they should not be adopted as the permanent metre of a national poem. The accents of a foreign metre do not settle in the ear or memory with domestic force; the hexameter, even if tolerable, may be monotonous or wearisome to ordinary readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use rhyme and native sound-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: It was a great error in an illustrious poet... to hate and banish rhyme. Rhyme is not merely an adventitious habit, it is founded on the very nature of Teutonic speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise native devices (alliteration, repetition of sound) and the historical transition to end-rhyme; avoid abandoning long-familiar rhyme forms (blank endings and unsatisfactory metres introduced by imitation of foreign models). Wieland's restoration of rhyme is praised as curing the mania for blank endings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate Christianity and northern (Gothic) mythology
rubrics_metrics.description: Christianity on the one hand, and Gothic mythology and antiquity on the other, must be the main elements of all new European poetry and inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small lyrical odes are insufficient to promote northern mythology; narrative and descriptive poetry (historic/romantic poems) are better instruments to revive and embed national mythic material into literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground poetry in actual life and precise mythology
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry 'too remote from actual life, and too devoid of any precise species of mythology' wanders in a world of shades and assumes tame uniformity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague, abstract 'worlds of shades.' Even if free of rhyme and metre can harmonize with such poetry, the lack of concrete mythic or life-based material promotes characteristic defects and uniform tameness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master the elegiac spirit where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Klopstock's most successful poetry is that conceived in the spirit of elegy. Every gradation, blending, and depth of elegiac feeling is handled by him with the power and ease of a master.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elegiac handling should move the reader's sympathies and guide them willingly through melancholy reflection. Where a poet excels in elegy, this may be the strongest aspect of their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid verbose and elaborate rhetorical excess in poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: In poetry he indulges in a verbose and elaborate species of rhetoric, which often destroys in a very great measure the effect of his feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-winded, frivolous conversations (even of elevated personages) weaken poetic feeling. Concision and avoiding ornamental prolixity preserve emotional impact; what is tolerable in one medium (prose sententiousness) may be damaging in poetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek harmony and unity in national literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who are best able to form an opinion... are sensible that its principal defect is its want of harmony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To remedy lack of harmony one must understand where harmony should be sought, follow the necessary paths, and beware of by-paths, obstacles, and dangers that interrupt unity across genres and periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance between extremes; aim for naturalness
rubrics_metrics.description: Between these two extremes of monotonous and uninteresting elevation, and luscious, half-Greek, half-modern effeminacy, the new poets endeavoured to establish something possessed of greater power, and more akin to nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid the two poles—either lofty monotonous elevation or artificial, effeminate prettiness—and strive for poetry rooted in living nature, with power, originality, and natural feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain purity of language
rubrics_metrics.description: They want, however, uniformity, regularity, and a standard: and are often chargeable with a neglect of the necessary purity of language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purity of language strengthens literature; some second-generation poets achieve strict purity. Yet excessive pedantry in language can render style painful or hard—balance precision with readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide uniformity and regularity without stifling originality
rubrics_metrics.description: The writers of this period... want uniformity, regularity, and a standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A literature benefits from standards and regularity to create coherence, but these should not suppress soul, fire, or originality; the ideal combines disciplined form with animated content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mine medieval and historical sources for national poetry
rubrics_metrics.description: He omitted... the whole middle age... the only one upon which poetry ever can be established so as to become a matter of historical and national influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical romantic poems (like Tasso's model) or works rooted in medieval materials often provide richer, more effective national poetry than purely fanciful or playful subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valourise energy and vivid poetical imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: The poem itself... has many errors and imperfections, but it must always retain its value as a poetical picture of great energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong pictorial energy and imaginative force can preserve a work's lasting value despite technical faults; striking imaginative effect matters greatly in evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer development of lofty poetry before establishing a national theatre
rubrics_metrics.description: A theatre cannot possibly assume an air of exquisite perfection, unless it has been preceded by a literature and poetry cultivated with high success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theatrical flourishing should follow rather than precede mature, lofty national poetry; an early national theatre risks shallowness if the broader literary foundations are not yet laid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism should learn from admiration of excellence, not only from detecting error
rubrics_metrics.description: We must learn to comprehend the essence of art from admiration of excellence, rather than from detection of error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critical practice that focuses chiefly on fault-finding (ascribed to Lessing) may miss the essence of art; critics should cultivate admiration and detailed study of perfections to assign true place and value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate imaginative empathy and universality of fancy
rubrics_metrics.description: The energy of fancy by which Herder was enabled to transport himself into the spirit and poetry of every age and people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A critic or poet should be able to enter into the shapes and manifestations of other ages/peoples; mythological feeling and empathetic imagination are distinguishing features of creative genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid philological bigotry and exclusionary dogma
rubrics_metrics.description: Such monstrous absurdities as confining the pure High Dutch language entirely to the limits of the old Margravate of Meissen, and of despising Klopstock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philological zeal must not become bigoted paradox; etymological or regional purism that dismisses genuine literary talent should be resisted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match metre and form to audience/readability
rubrics_metrics.description: The hexameter, when carelessly executed, displeases scholars, and when written with accuracy, appears monotonous and wearisome to ordinary readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing a measure consider both scholarly reception and popular accessibility; a technically perfect foreign metre may still alienate general readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use foreign forms as exercises, not permanent practice
rubrics_metrics.description: With whatever excellent effects the introduction of foreign forms may be attended, they should be still regarded merely as exercises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign metres and elaborate imports can correct laxity and develop skill, but should not replace measures and forms rooted in national speech and tradition.
